title: Training Q&A — True-Up Reserve Held from a Utility Pass-Through Service Credit Refund After an Estimated Read
content:
**Rule.** When a credit balance on a final-billed Utility Pass-Through Service account is refunded and the latest water read on the account is an estimated read, a true-up reserve of 50 percent of the reserve base is held when no more than 30 days have passed since that read's date and of 25 percent when 31 to 60 days have passed; no reserve is held where the latest water read is not an estimated read or more than 60 days have passed since it; the reserve is rounded half up to the cent. A reserve held is deducted from the credit balance as well.

## Questions answered

**Q. Which read decides?** The latest water read on the account — the water read with the latest read date. Only when that read is an estimated read can a reserve be held.

**Q. How are the days counted?** The handling date less that read's date.

**Q. What is the reserve base?** The water usage charge amount the true-up reserve is measured on.

**Q. The rates at a glance?**

| Latest water read | Days since its date | Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Estimated | 0 to 30 | 50 percent of the reserve base |
| Estimated | 31 to 60 | 25 percent of the reserve base |
| Estimated | 61 or more | none |
| Not an estimate (actual, final or re-read) | any | none |

**Q. Worked through (hypothetical reserve base 33.62).** Estimated read 30 days old: 50 percent is 16.81. Estimated read 31 days old: 25 percent is 8.405, rounded half up to 8.41. A credit balance of 120.00 with the 16.81 reserve held leaves 103.19 before any other deduction.
